chapter_seo_title: Dao Guai Yi Xian Ch. 263: A Scholar's Resentment Boils Over
chapter_meta_description: Lyu Xiucai's envy reaches a breaking point. He steals Li Huowang's sword, claiming to have gained supernatural powers. A brutal confrontation and a chilling prophecy of violence follow.
og_title: The Ambition of a Scholar Can Be a Poison
og_description: A quiet dinner of knife-cut noodles explodes into violence when a desperate teenager tries to claim a power that was never his to take.
twitter_title: A scholar's dream becomes a nightmare in Ch. 263!
twitter_description: Lyu Xiucai's desperate grab for power ends in a brutal whipping and a chilling death threat. A key turning point for the group.

lore_anchors.definition: In imperial China, a scholar who passed the first level of the civil service examinations. The title granted status but rarely wealth, creating a class of educated, frustrated men.
A traditional Chinese noodle dish from Shanxi, made by slicing strips of dough directly into boiling water.
A likely borrowed or gifted weapon, noted for its strong killing intent. Its origin and full history remain mysterious.
A tangible, often overwhelming aura of lethal desire that can emanate from powerful weapons or cultivators, affecting those who are not strong enough to bear it.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can't Li Huowang teach his 'supernatural ability' to others?
cultural_notes_faq.a: His power is tied to unique circumstances (being a Heart-Element, having Danyangzi inside him) and isn't a transferable skill or technique.
It's a powerful, unnamed weapon given to Li Huowang by a nun from Anci Nunnery. It's noted for its strong killing intent, which Lyu Xiucai cannot handle.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Will Lyu Xiucai become a major threat later?
cultural_notes_faq.a: His desire for power and his humiliation at being beaten are strong motivators. The way the author frames his resentment suggests he may not stay a harmless background character for long.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Lyu Xiucai's title as a 'Scholar' important?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It represents a class of educated, ambitious men in feudal China who were often left powerless and resentful. His frustration is a personal and a social commentary.
